title: Retail inflation hits 6.09% in October, breaching RBI's upper limit as food prices jump
dek: Food inflation rose to 8.94%, led by onion and garlic. Economists expect a second straight repo rate hike in December. Earlier, the Sensex and Nifty ended barely higher and the rupee fell 33 paise to 94.04.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
India's retail inflation rose to 6.09% in October from 5.54% in September, breaching the upper limit of the Reserve Bank of India's 2-6% tolerance band, as food prices climbed faster, according to provisional data released by the National Statistics Office (NSO) on Thursday evening. The reading is the highest in about two years and strengthens the case for a second successive increase in interest rates in December.

Food inflation, measured by the Consumer Food Price Index, rose to 8.94% from 7.74% in September, reports of the release said. Inflation in rural areas was 6.63%, up from 6.08%, and in urban areas 5.41%, up from 4.88%. Economists polled before the release had expected a headline figure of about 6%.

## What drove it

Vegetables and spices led the rise. Onion prices were 116.22% higher than a year earlier and garlic 60.74% higher, while ginger and lemons were up by more than 47%, according to the item-wise data as reported. Potato prices were 14.24% lower. Among the broad groups, restaurants and accommodation rose 10.06% and clothing and footwear 4.96%, while housing (2.90%) and health (2.05%) stayed low. Silver jewellery inflation eased to 52.39% from 87.80%.

The figures are on the new consumer price index series with 2024 as its base year, which the government introduced this year. They are provisional and may be revised next month.

## What it means for interest rates

The RBI's Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) raised the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50% on 7 October, its first increase since February 2023, and changed its stance to what it called "calibrated tightening". Its target is 4% inflation, within a band of 2% to 6%. A single month above 6% is not a formal breach of the mandate, which requires inflation to average more than 6% for three consecutive quarters.

"The data reinforces our expectation of a second successive rate hike in December," said Radhika Rao, senior economist at DBS Bank, according to reports. Tanay Dalal of Axis Bank said the numbers raised the risk that rates "may need to rise above the estimated neutral rate of 6%", reports said. Vikram Chhabra of 360 ONE Asset said there were "clear signs of broadening inflationary pressures".

## Markets

The data came after markets closed. In a volatile session, the BSE Sensex ended 31.61 points, or 0.04%, higher at 81,911.01, and the NSE Nifty 50 rose 44.30 points, or 0.18%, to 25,299.35, according to market reports. Mid-cap and small-cap shares did better, rising 0.85% and 1.12%. Realty stocks gained about 4%, while auto, consumer goods and IT shares fell. HDFC Life was the biggest gainer in the Nifty and Nestle India the biggest loser. Page Industries fell about 13% after its quarterly results.

Analysts said the market was pausing after a rally of about 10% this month, supported by heavy buying by foreign portfolio investors and a fall in oil prices. Brent crude fell more than 1% to about $92 a barrel on hopes of diplomacy in West Asia. "Softer crude provided macro relief," said Vinod Nair of Geojit Investments.

The rupee closed 33 paise lower at 94.04 to the US dollar, according to reports, from 93.71 on Wednesday, as the dollar strengthened abroad.

## What happens next

The MPC meets from 2 to 4 December and announces its decision on 4 December. Inflation data for November are due on 14 December. Friday's trading session will be the first market reaction to the October figures.
